facts.claim: BIAAPA Master Plan 2021 covers about 228 villages around KIA and is administered under the Karnataka Town & Country Planning Act 1961. Zones are residential, commercial, industrial, public utility and green, each with its own FAR, setbacks and permitted uses. A plot shown as residential still needs a formal Change of Land Use (CLU) order before construction; CLU takes up to about 60 days.
facts.source_title: 1acre.in - BIAAPA Masterplan 2021: North Bengaluru Airport Area Zone Check

facts.claim: BIAAPA's Master Plan 2021 is reported to include colour-coded zones around the KIA runways with strict building-height limits. CLU goes through public notice, then BIAAPA, then BMRDA, then a state government decision.
facts.source_title: Landeed - BIAAPA Zones in Bangalore: What It Means for Your Construction

facts.claim: A Karnataka Legislative Council paper says BIAAPA has started revising its Master Plan, i.e. preparing a Revised Master Plan-2031. A 2018 report says BIAAPA would hire consultants to prepare the revised plan. No published or approved RMP-2031/2041 was found.

facts.claim: KIA has two parallel runways, 09L/27R (north, the original runway) and 09R/27L (south). Each is 4,000 m long and 45 m wide. The south runway was commissioned on 6 Dec 2019, making KIA the first Indian airport with independent parallel runways.
facts.source_title: Airport Technology - Kempegowda International Airport begins second runway operations

facts.claim: Airport elevation is about 915 m (3,002 ft) AMSL (Wikipedia, AC-U-KWIK). Sprinkle.com gives 3,000 ft (914.4 m).

facts.claim: Approximate threshold coordinates from a single non-official source: 09L 13.2072N 77.6861E; 27R 13.2068N 77.7230E; 09R 13.1897N 77.6900E; 27L 13.1894N 77.7269E. ARP 13.1979N 77.7063E. Not cross-checked against AIP India, which could not be reached. The 4.0 km runway length computed from these points matches the published length.
facts.source_title: sprinkle.com - VOBL airport data

facts.claim: KIA runway headings are 092 deg / 272 deg.
facts.source_title: SkyVector - VOBL

facts.claim: DERIVED from the threshold coordinates above. The site centroid (13.200277N, 77.650030E) is about 3.98 km west of the 09L threshold and 0.81 km south of the 09L/27R extended centreline. It is about 4.48 km from the 09R threshold and 1.13 km north of the 09R/27L extended centreline. The centroid is about 6.1 km from the ARP. The site sits between the two extended centrelines, under the western (arrival-to-09 / departure-from-27) approach and take-off corridors.
facts.value: 3.98 km to 09L threshold; 0.81 km off 09L centreline
facts.source_title: Researcher calculation from sprinkle.com coordinates

facts.claim: DERIVED, assuming standard ICAO Annex 14 code-4 precision approach geometry (inner edge 300 m wide, 60 m before threshold, 15% divergence each side, 2% slope for the first 3,000 m then 2.5%), which was NOT verified against Indian rules in this study. At 3.9 km before 09L the approach surface half-width is about 726 m, so the centroid (809 m off centreline) is just outside it. A 31 ha parcel (~550 m across) probably straddles its southern edge. At that distance the approach surface is about 81 m above threshold elevation. The site is also within about 4 km of the 09L strip end, so the inner horizontal surface (45 m above aerodrome elevation, 4,000 m radius per ICAO tables) is likely the lower and governing limit. That implies roughly 960 m AMSL as an indicative ceiling, before any CCZM value. The binding figure must come from the AAI NOCAS CCZM grid.
facts.value: indicative ceiling about 45 m above aerodrome elevation (~960 m AMSL); unverified
facts.source_title: Uganda CAA ICAO-derived OLS table (inner horizontal 45 m / 4000 m)

facts.claim: G.S.R. 751(E), dated 30 Sep 2015, is the Ministry of Civil Aviation (Height Restrictions for Safeguarding of Aircraft Operations) Rules, 2015. They apply to the civil and defence aerodromes listed in Schedules III-VII, as amended. A bilingual gazette PDF is on the MoCA website. The specific approach-slope figures (2%, 15% divergence) were not confirmed from the rule text.
facts.source_title: Ministry of Civil Aviation - Gazette Notification (Height Restrictions) Rules 2015

facts.claim: AAI issues Colour Coded Zoning Maps (CCZM) under Rule 6 of the 2015 Rules, covering a 20 km radius around each aerodrome. Applicants find the plot's grid from WGS-84 coordinates and read the Permissible Top Elevation (m AMSL). Red-coded grids need an AAI NOC via NOCAS (nocas2.aai.aero), and the local body cannot approve them directly.
facts.source_title: MCGM - AAI Guidelines for CCZM; verified.realestate - Decoding Airport CCZM

facts.claim: The actual CCZM Permissible Top Elevation for Sadahalli grid cells was not retrieved; the NOCAS portal was not reachable. Sadahalli lies within the 20 km CCZM radius (about 6 km from the ARP), so an AAI NOC is required.

summary: Site 4 sits under the western approach and departure corridors of KIA: by calculation from non-official threshold coordinates, the centroid is about 4.0 km west of the 09L threshold and about 0.8 km south of the north runway's extended centreline. It is probably at the edge of the 09L approach surface and well within the roughly 4 km inner-horizontal zone. Building height will therefore be capped by the AAI CCZM/NOC process under GSR 751(E). An indicative ICAO-based ceiling is about 45 m above aerodrome elevation (~960 m AMSL), but the binding NOCAS grid value was not retrieved. Planning is under BIAAPA RMP-2021. A revision to RMP-2031 has been started but not published, and the zone for the six survey numbers, plus the BIAAPA FAR, setback and height tables, could not be found online. These need a BIAAPA zonal certificate and possibly a CLU. Access is strong: the site is next to the NH-44 Sadahalli toll and junction (a Rs 35 crore underpass is planned), the STRR has been open since 2024, and the planned Doddajala metro station on Blue Line Phase 2B is about 1.4 km away. Phase 2B opening is expected in 2027-28, not 2026. Groundwater is a major constraint: Devanahalli taluk is Over-Exploited at 169% (2024), the shallow aquifer is desaturated, and there is no perennial or Cauvery source, so water strategy (treated water, HN Valley recharge, harvesting) is critical. Nearby demand drivers include the Aerospace Park and SEZ, Devanahalli Business Park, ITIR/Foxconn, Bhartiya City and pre-launch Lodha and Prestige projects at Sadahalli Gate. Aerospace expansion acquisition of 1,777 acres was withdrawn in Dec 2025.
